summary: Michel Clasquin is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied and completed his doctoral thesis at the University of South Africa between circa 1989 and 1999, and held a post there in 1990.

Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Geneva, where he was an assistant (1987–1992), and later served at Hanazono University and the University of Hawaii.

Michel Strickmann specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned diplomas and doctorates at EPHE and Paris Diderot University under supervisors including Kristofer Schipper, Maxime Kaltenmark, and Léon Vandermeersch, later holding posts at UC Berkeley and Bordeaux.
Michela Clemente works in the field of Tibetology. She studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger, and served as a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.
Michele Kerbaker was an Indologist and linguist. He succeeded Giacomo Lignana in 1870 and held a post at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" from circa 1872 to 1914.

Michelle C. Wang specializes in art history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her doctorate under Eugene Y. Wang and served as an assistant professor of art and art history at Georgetown University from circa 2012 to 2018.
Michelle Spuler is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Queensland (~1997–2000) and taught at Colorado College and Victoria University of Wellington.

Michihiko Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He served at Taisho University as an assistant (attested 1978–1980) and professor (attested 2014–2015), and chaired the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies.

Michihiko Yajima specializes in Indology and linguistics. He completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo, where he held an attested post in 1992, and later served as a professor at Tsurumi University (attested 2003–2008).

Michihiro Ikeda works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has held positions at Setagaya Gakuen High School, Komazawa Junior College, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Michiko Yusa is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. She completed her Ph.D. at UC Santa Barbara under Raimon Panikkar and served as a professor of foreign languages at Western Washington University from circa 1983 to 2021.
Michio Kamikawa is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ritsumeikan University and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University around 1998.

Michio Yano specializes in Indology and history. He studied at Kyoto University and Brown University under David Pingree, and served as a professor in the Faculty of Cultural Studies at Kyoto Sangyo University from 1974 to 2014.

Michitoshi Barada specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi, researched at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1997, and held posts at Otani University and the Eastern Institute.
Michiya Ito studied as a graduate student at Tohoku University from 1986 to 1990 and later held a post there between 2001 and 2004.
Michiyo Hoshi is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. She has held research posts at the Toyo Bunko and the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa.
Midori Nishino works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and later served as a researcher there (attested 2010–2015).

Migmar Tsering was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He headed Sakya College (attested 1991–1997) and held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Mikaël Bauer specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University under Ryuichi Abe.

Mikel Burley works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Essex and Bristol under J. M. Bernstein, Jonardon Ganeri, Brian Carr, and John Peacock, and became an associate professor at the University of Leeds.
